jail.finding: The message asks for $2,000 in gift cards. Real jails, lawyers, and courts never take gift cards. Only scammers ask for them.

steps.title: Don't send any more money
steps.detail: Don't send the rest of the $2,000. Don't reply to the message. If they ask for more, or call back with a 'lawyer' or 'police officer', just hang up.

steps.title: Call the gift card company right now
steps.detail: Look at the back of the gift card or the card holder for the company's phone number, or go to the company's official website. Tell them you were scammed and ask them to freeze the money on the card. The faster you call, the better your chances.

steps.title: Keep the card and the receipt
steps.detail: Don't throw away the card, its packaging, or the store receipt. The gift card company needs the card number and receipt to help you.

steps.title: Call your grandchild yourself
steps.detail: Call your grandchild, or their parent, on the phone number you already have. You will most likely find out they are safe and not in jail.

steps.title: Save the message
steps.detail: Don't delete the message. Take a picture or screenshot of it, and write down the number it came from and when you sent the card.

steps.title: Report it
steps.detail: Report it to the FTC and the FBI using the forms below. You can copy the ready-made text into the forms. Reporting helps stop these scammers.
